\begin{abstract}
We certify the original polynomial-coefficient recurrences conjectured by
Kauers and Zeilberger for diagonal rook walks in every dimension
$d=4,\ldots,12$. This supplies a computer-assisted solution of the finite
certification question stated as Problem~17 by Chen and Kauers.
The argument represents the diagonal coefficients as powers of a Laguerre
polynomial integrated against an exponential weight. Integration by parts
reduces all required shifted integrals to a family of $d$ moments.
For each original recurrence, its residual is then checked to be the zero
vector over $\Q[n]$, after clearing explicitly known denominators.
The initial index $n=0$ is checked separately from a finite combinatorial
formula. Thus the conclusion holds for every nonnegative index, without
an interpolation assumption, a modular reconstruction assumption, or an
unproved minimal-order assertion. The integral reduction was established in
corpus manuscript~[067]; the contribution here is the direct exact
certification of the published equations, including its five remaining
dimensions $8$ through $12$. The single-file source contains the original
data and a reproducible verifier. No claim of an unprecedented general
principle or of universal recurrence minimality is made.
\end{abstract}

\section{The original problem and the precise result}
Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diag}
 R_d(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=
 \frac{1}{1-\sum_{i=1}^d x_i/(1-x_i)},\qquad
 a_n^{(d)}=[x_1^n\cdots x_d^n]R_d.
\end{equation}
In particular $a_0^{(d)}=1$. These integers count paths from
$(0,\ldots,0)$ to $(n,\ldots,n)$, each step increasing exactly one coordinate
by an arbitrary positive integer.

Kauers and Zeilberger~\cite{KZ} published conjectured recurrences for
these sequences through dimension twelve in 2010. Their computational
challenge was to obtain rigorous certificates for those specific
equations. Chen and Kauers~\cite[Problem~17]{CK} subsequently asked for
proofs in dimensions $4,\ldots,12$. This is an existing numbered problem
in symbolic computation, not an Erd\H{o}s problem. It asks for the
published equations themselves; merely proving the existence of some
recurrence would not answer it.

Write the authors' equations in forward-shift form as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:target}
 \sum_{j=0}^d K_{d,j}(n)a_{n+j}^{(d)}=0,
 \qquad K_{d,j}\in\Z[n].
\end{equation}
Here the $K_{d,j}$ are the actual coefficients in the original public
data~\cite{data}, expanded without changing their normalization.
Their complete integer coefficient lists are included in the source
payload described in Section~\ref{sec:repro}. The input hashes in that
payload fix the precise source bytes; the coefficient hashes also fix
the expanded polynomials. This is important because the largest list
contains coefficients of more than two thousand bits.

\begin{theorem}[Certification of the original equations]\label{thm:main}
For each $d\in\{4,5,\ldots,12\}$, the original Kauers--Zeilberger
polynomials $K_{d,0},\ldots,K_{d,d}$ satisfy \eqref{eq:target} for
every integer $n\ge0$.
\end{theorem}

The proof consists of the analytic identities established below and
finite exact polynomial calculations. Every coordinate of every cleared
residual is verified to be identically zero, not only zero at some
sample indices. Dimensions two and three are included as consistency
checks and are not claimed as new results.

\subsection{Relation to previous work}
The three-dimensional recurrence was proved by Bostan, Chyzak,
van Hoeij and Pech~\cite{BCvHP}. The general idea of combining an a priori
bound with exact algebraic verification was already proposed in
\cite[Section~2]{KZ}; reduction methods for rational integrals also have
substantial prior literature, including~\cite{BLS,Lairez}.
The supplied corpus manuscript~[067]~\cite{corpus} develops the particular
Laguerre moment reduction used here, proves an order-at-most-$d$ theorem
for every dimension, and reports certification through dimension seven.
It explicitly leaves the original equations for dimensions eight through
twelve uncertified. We credit that reduction and reproduce its proof so
that the present certification is self-contained.

Our additional step is to construct the denominator-cleared reduction
vectors directly over $\Q[n]$ and apply them to the original published
coefficient lists. This eliminates the previous identification through
guessed uniqueness and completes all the dimensions requested in
Problem~17. The novelty asserted is this certification result and its
reproducible implementation, not the underlying integration-by-parts
principle. A targeted literature review on the date of this manuscript
did not locate an earlier full certification of dimensions eight through
twelve. That review is not a proof of absolute historical priority.

\section{A one-variable integral for the diagonal}
For $n\ge1$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ell}
 \ell_n(s)=\sum_{k=1}^n\binom{n-1}{k-1}\frac{s^k}{k!}.
\end{equation}
This is $L_n^{(-1)}(-s)$ in the usual Laguerre notation, but no facts
about special functions will be required beyond the identities proved
here.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:integral}
For every $d\ge1$ and $n\ge1$,
\begin{align}
 a_n^{(d)}
 &=\sum_{1\le k_1,\ldots,k_d\le n}
   \frac{(k_1+\cdots+k_d)!}{k_1!\cdots k_d!}
   \prod_{h=1}^d\binom{n-1}{k_h-1}\label{eq:finite}\\
 &=\int_0^\infty e^{-s}\ell_n(s)^d\,ds.\label{eq:integral}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand the geometric series in \eqref{eq:diag} and then use the
multinomial theorem. For $n\ge1$,
\[
 [x^n]\left(\frac{x}{1-x}\right)^k
 =\binom{n-1}{k-1}\quad(1\le k\le n),
\]
and the coefficient is zero for $k=0$ and for $k>n$. Hence coefficient
extraction leaves exactly the finite sum \eqref{eq:finite}.
Replacing $(k_1+\cdots+k_d)!$ by
$\int_0^\infty e^{-s}s^{k_1+\cdots+k_d}\,ds$ and factoring the finite
sum gives \eqref{eq:integral}. There is no interchange of infinite
sums with an integral.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:identities}
The following identities hold for $n\ge1$:
\begin{align}
 &\ell_n(0)=0,\qquad \ell_n'(0)=1,\label{eq:endpoint}\\
 &s\ell_n''+s\ell_n'-n\ell_n=0,\label{eq:ode}\\
 &(n+1)\ell_{n+1}=(n+s)\ell_n+s\ell_n',\qquad
   \ell_{n+1}'=\ell_n+\ell_n'.\label{eq:shift}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first assertion follows from the first term of \eqref{eq:ell}.
Put $c_k=\binom{n-1}{k-1}/k!$, taking coefficients outside the allowed
range to be zero. The coefficient of $s^k$ in \eqref{eq:ode} is
$(k+1)k c_{k+1}+(k-n)c_k=0$ by the adjacent-binomial identity.
For the first shift identity its coefficient of $s^k$ is
$(n+k)c_k+c_{k-1}=(n+1)\binom n{k-1}/k!$; the endpoint
$k=n+1$ has coefficient $1/n!$ on both sides. The second shift identity
is Pascal's identity, after comparing coefficients of $s^{k-1}$.
\end{proof}

\section{The auxiliary moment reduction problem}
Fix $d\ge1$. For $0\le i\le d$ and $k\ge i-d$ put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:J}
 J_n(i,k)=\int_0^\infty e^{-s}s^k
             \ell_n(s)^{d-i}\ell_n'(s)^i\,ds.
\end{equation}
The integrand is $O(s^{k+d-i})$ near zero and decays exponentially
times a polynomial at infinity, so it is integrable. Negative powers
of $s$ in this notation cause no divergence in the stated range.

The auxiliary problem is to express every $J_n(i,k)$ with $k\ge0$
using a fixed finite family of moments, with coefficients polynomial in
$n$. Its solution supplies a certificate space for the original
recurrence problem. The family is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:family}
 J_n(0,1-d),\ J_n(0,2-d),\ldots,J_n(0,0).
\end{equation}
We do not assume these $d$ quantities are linearly independent.

\begin{lemma}[Integration by parts]\label{lem:ibp}
If $0\le i\le d$ and $k\ge i-d+1$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ibp}
 (i+1)J_n(i,k)=kJ_n(i,k-1)+(d-i)J_n(i+1,k)
                       +inJ_n(i-1,k-1),
\end{equation}
where terms with zero coefficient are omitted.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $m_i=\ell_n^{d-i}(\ell_n')^i$. Equation~\eqref{eq:ode} gives
$m_i'=(d-i)m_{i+1}+in\,m_{i-1}/s-im_i$.
The function $e^{-s}s^k m_i$ vanishes at both endpoints: at zero its
order is at least $k+d-i\ge1$. Every nonzero term in its derivative
is integrable, since its lowest possible order at zero is
$k+d-i-1\ge0$. Integrating that derivative proves \eqref{eq:ibp}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial reduction]\label{lem:reduction}
For $0\le i\le d$, $k\ge0$, there are effectively computable
$\gamma_b^{(i,k)}(n)\in\Q[n]$, $1-d\le b\le0$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma}
 J_n(i,k)=\sum_{b=1-d}^0\gamma_b^{(i,k)}(n)J_n(0,b)
 \quad(n\ge1).
\end{equation}
All divisions in their construction are by nonzero integers depending
on $d$ and $i$, not by functions of $n$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We give the elimination and its boundary cancellations explicitly.
For $1\le i\le d$, applying \eqref{eq:ibp} with $i-1$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lower}
 (d-i+1)J_n(i,k)
 =iJ_n(i-1,k)-kJ_n(i-1,k-1)-(i-1)nJ_n(i-2,k-1).
\end{equation}
It is valid whenever $k\ge i-d$. Terms of index $i-2$ are omitted
when their coefficient is zero. Induction on $i$ expresses this as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda}
 J_n(i,k)=\sum_{b=k-i}^k\lambda_b^{(i,k)}(n)J_n(0,b),
\end{equation}
with polynomial coefficients. Only the first term on the right of
\eqref{eq:lower} contributes to the largest index; only its second
term contributes to the smallest. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda-ends}
 \lambda_k^{(i,k)}=\binom di^{-1},\qquad
 \lambda_{k-i}^{(i,k)}=(-1)^i\binom ki\binom di^{-1}.
\end{equation}
For integer $k$, the binomial coefficient here means the falling
factorial polynomial $k(k-1)\cdots(k-i+1)/i!$, so the formula also
covers negative $k$.

Next take $i=d$ and $k\ge1$ in \eqref{eq:ibp}, and substitute
\eqref{eq:lambda}. Since $\lambda_k^{(d,k)}=1$, this expresses
$J_n(0,k)$ as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mu}
 J_n(0,k)=\sum_{b=k-d-1}^{k-1}\mu_b^{(k)}(n)J_n(0,b),
 \qquad
 \mu_{k-d-1}^{(k)}=\frac{(-1)^d k}{d+1}\binom{k-1}{d}.
\end{equation}
The last coefficient vanishes for $1\le k\le d$. In this range the
remaining indices are at least $k-d\ge1-d$; for $k\ge d+1$ all
indices are nonnegative and smaller than $k$. Induction on $k$ now
reduces all $J_n(0,k)$ with $k\ge1-d$ into \eqref{eq:family}.

Finally, for $k\ge0$ the smallest index in \eqref{eq:lambda} is
$k-i\ge-d$. The value $-d$ is possible only if $(i,k)=(d,0)$, where
its coefficient is $(-1)^d\binom0d=0$. Thus no extra moment is
needed. The elimination divides only by $d-i+1$ and $d+1$, proving
the last assertion as well.
\end{proof}

\section{Shift transport and exact polynomial certificates}
Define $P_0(n)=1$ and $P_j(n)=\prod_{r=1}^j(n+r)$. Repeated use of
\eqref{eq:shift} gives polynomial matrices
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix}
 P_j(n)\begin{pmatrix}\ell_{n+j}\\\ell_{n+j}'\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}A_j&B_j\\C_j&D_j\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}\ell_n\\\ell_n'\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
All entries belong to $\Z[n,s]$. Start with $A_0=D_0=1$ and
$B_0=C_0=0$; the complete recursion is
\begin{align}
 A_{j+1}&=(n+j+s)A_j+sC_j,&
 B_{j+1}&=(n+j+s)B_j+sD_j,\label{eq:AB}\\
 C_{j+1}&=(n+j+1)(A_j+C_j),&
 D_{j+1}&=(n+j+1)(B_j+D_j).\label{eq:CD}
\end{align}
It follows by induction that each entry has total degree at most $j$
in $n,s$.

Expanding the $d$th power of the first row and applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:reduction} defines polynomials
\begin{equation}\label{eq:W}
 W_{j,b}(n)=\sum_{i=0}^d\binom di
   \sum_{k\ge0}[s^k](A_j^{d-i}B_j^i)\,
                        \gamma_b^{(i,k)}(n),
 \qquad 1-d\le b\le0.
\end{equation}
The sums are finite, with $k\le dj$. Equations~\eqref{eq:integral}
and \eqref{eq:matrix} give the exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:shifted-integral}
 P_j(n)^d a_{n+j}^{(d)}
   =\sum_{b=1-d}^0W_{j,b}(n)J_n(0,b)\quad(n\ge1).
\end{equation}
These $W$ vectors can be constructed without any sequence values and
without guessing a recurrence.

\begin{theorem}[Sufficient polynomial certificate]\label{thm:certificate}
Let $K_0,\ldots,K_d\in\Q[n]$. Construct $W$ as in \eqref{eq:W} and
form the $d$ polynomials
\begin{equation}\label{eq:residual}
 T_b(n)=\sum_{j=0}^d K_j(n)
            \left(\frac{P_d(n)}{P_j(n)}\right)^d W_{j,b}(n),
 \qquad 1-d\le b\le0.
\end{equation}
If all $T_b$ are the zero polynomial, then
$\sum_{j=0}^dK_j(n)a_{n+j}^{(d)}=0$ for every integer $n\ge1$.
If additionally $\sum_{j=0}^dK_j(0)a_j^{(d)}=0$, the same recurrence
holds for every integer $n\ge0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Multiply the claimed recurrence by $P_d(n)^d$ and substitute
\eqref{eq:shifted-integral}. The result is
\[
 \sum_{b=1-d}^0T_b(n)J_n(0,b)=0.
\]
Every factor of $P_d(n)$ is a positive integer for $n\ge1$, so it
can be divided out. The additional hypothesis is exactly the missing
index $n=0$. No leading coefficient of the recurrence is divided out,
so possible singular indices of that coefficient cause no exception.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Vanishing of all the coordinate polynomials is a sufficient
certificate; it is not asserted to be necessary for every identity
among these integrals. Linear independence of the retained moments
is unnecessary. Nor does the theorem assume that a guessed relation
of a given order or degree is unique.
\end{remark}

\subsection{An optional finite-evaluation bound}
The following bound from the same reduction explains why exact
evaluation could also certify a candidate. The computations for the
main theorem use direct symbolic vanishing instead.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:degree}
Put $e=\lceil d/2\rceil$. Then
\[
 \degN W_{j,b}\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor+edj.
\]
If $\max_j\deg K_j\le D$, every polynomial in \eqref{eq:residual}
has degree at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bound}
 B_d(D)=D+\lfloor d/2\rfloor+\lceil d/2\rceil d^2.
\end{equation}
In particular $B_d(D)+1$ exact zero evaluations at distinct positive
integers for each coordinate are sufficient.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
In \eqref{eq:lower}, only the term with index $i-2$ introduces a
factor $n$. Therefore $\degN\lambda_b^{(i,k)}\le\lfloor i/2\rfloor$.
Formula~\eqref{eq:mu} has coefficient degrees at most
$\max(\lfloor d/2\rfloor,1+\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor)=e$.
Induction in $k$ bounds the degree of a reduced coordinate of
$J_n(0,k)$ by $ek$ for $k\ge0$. Lowering $i$ first then gives
$\degN\gamma_b^{(i,k)}\le\lfloor i/2\rfloor+ek$.
Indeed, retained negative base indices have constant coordinates, and
every intermediate index $h$ satisfies $\max(0,h)\le k$.

Since $A_j,B_j$ have total degree at most $j$, the coefficient
$[s^k](A_j^{d-i}B_j^i)$ has $n$-degree at most $dj-k$.
Each summand in \eqref{eq:W} therefore has degree at most
$dj-k+\lfloor i/2\rfloor+ek\le\lfloor d/2\rfloor+edj$.
In \eqref{eq:residual}, the extra factor $(P_d/P_j)^d$ has degree
$d(d-j)$. Maximizing
$D+d(d-j)+\lfloor d/2\rfloor+edj$ over $0\le j\le d$
gives \eqref{eq:bound}. A polynomial with more roots than its degree
is identically zero.
\end{proof}

\section{Certification of the published coefficient lists}\label{sec:compute}
For $d\le9$ we used the authors' Maple aggregate
\texttt{ManuelRookRecurrences}; for $d=10,11,12$ we used the original
files \texttt{rooks10-rec.m}, \texttt{rooks11-rec.m}, and
\texttt{rooks12-rec.m}. The aggregate contains the same displayed
forward shifts $f[n+j]$. The parser allows only integer constants,
the indeterminate $n$, parentheses, signs, addition, multiplication,
and nonnegative integer powers. It checks the shift expression and
that every shift occurs exactly once. It neither runs Maple nor
executes the source as a program.

The coefficient lists are converted into exact integer polynomials.
The moments and shifts are calculated over $\Q[n]$ using
\texttt{python-flint}~0.9.0. For each $b$, equality of $T_b$ with zero
means equality of its entire normalized rational-polynomial object
with zero; no floating-point operation or prime-modular inference is
used. Exact polynomial quotients $P_d/P_j$ are available because
these products are explicitly nested.

For the remaining index $n=0$, use $a_0^{(d)}=1$ and let
\[
 G_n(s)=n!\ell_n(s)\in\Z[s],\qquad
 a_n^{(d)}=\frac{\sum_{h=0}^{dn}h![s^h]G_n(s)^d}{(n!)^d}
 \quad(n\ge1).
\]
The verifier computes this finite sum exactly for $1\le n\le d+2$
and checks the original equation at zero, together with the additional
consistency checks at $n=1,2$.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}]
The original coefficient lists give the degrees and bit lengths in
Table~\ref{tab:results}. The exact verifier reproduced in the source
constructs \eqref{eq:W} and obtains $T_b=0$ for every one of the
$d$ coordinates in each dimension $4\le d\le12$. It also obtains
zero for the independently computed $n=0$ equation in every case.
These are finite rational-arithmetic identities with the full inputs
provided. Theorem~\ref{thm:certificate} applies to each list and
proves the original equation for every nonnegative integer index.
\end{proof}

For orientation, the two-dimensional input is
\[
 (n+2)a_{n+2}^{(2)}-(10n+14)a_{n+1}^{(2)}+9na_n^{(2)}=0.
\]
Here $a_0,a_1,a_2=1,2,14$, and the zero-index check is
$2\cdot14-14\cdot2=0$. The high-dimensional checks use precisely
the same logical steps, with larger input polynomials.

\subsection{Independent verification and computational scope}
The cleared symbolic construction was cross-checked against a
numerical exact-rational moment reduction at $n=1,3$ in every
dimension two through twelve. A separate implementation of the
literal $\lambda$ and $\mu$ recursions agreed with the reduced vectors
at $n=1,2,7$ in those dimensions. These comparisons detect
implementation errors but are not substituted for the polynomial
identities used in the proof.

In addition, a second complete symbolic implementation was run for
every dimension $8,9,10,11,12$. It constructs the literal $\lambda$
coefficients and then the $\mu$ reduction, and transports shifts using
the three-term identity
\[
 (n+1)\ell_{n+1}=(2n+s)\ell_n-(n-1)\ell_{n-1}
 \qquad(n\ge2).
\]
The initial forward shift is obtained from \eqref{eq:shift}.
All residual polynomials again vanished exactly, and separate
zero-index checks passed. Its independently parsed input polynomials
agreed with the supplied coefficient lists. The independent checker
and its successful log are retained in the source payload.

The initial symbolic run took approximately $1.2$, $3.0$, $8.3$,
$17.3$, and $43.8$ seconds for dimensions eight through twelve,
including the first cross-checks and the zero-index checks, on the
research execution environment. These are observed timings, not
hardware-independent complexity claims. In particular, construction
of the certificate does not require the hundreds of large sequence
values needed for guessing or long finite-evaluation runs.

\section{Reproducibility and data identity}\label{sec:repro}
The accompanying single \texttt{.tex} file is both the complete
typesetting source and a container for the proof inputs. After
\verb|\end{document}| it contains an ASCII-encoded compressed
payload, bounded by the comment markers
\texttt{ROOK-PAYLOAD-BEGIN} and \texttt{ROOK-PAYLOAD-END}.
This payload includes the original authors' source bytes, the
expanded coefficient lists, source URLs and SHA-256 digests, and
the standalone exact verifier. The payload is ignored by TeX;
compiling the paper requires no external data file or bibliography.
The distributed PDF also carries this ZIP as an embedded attachment. The single-file TeX source is sufficient to recover it independently. Its contents are extracted for verification as follows.

\begin{lstlisting}
# Save as extract_rook.py; run:
# python extract_rook.py PAPER.tex
from pathlib import Path
import base64, hashlib, io, sys, zipfile

lines = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="ascii").splitlines()
first = lines.index("% ROOK-PAYLOAD-BEGIN") + 1
last = lines.index("% ROOK-PAYLOAD-END")
encoded = "".join(line[2:] for line in lines[first:last])
payload = base64.b85decode(encoded)
expected = ("21bf5366e6df90c2d746e4cf22948353d"
            "7913a901577bd66222f134d09591b0d")
assert hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() == expected
target = Path("rook_certificate")
target.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(payload)) as archive:
    for name in archive.namelist():
        assert Path(name).name == name
        (target / name).write_bytes(archive.read(name))
# Then run:
# python rook_certificate/verify_rook.py \
#   --data rook_certificate/certificate_data.json
\end{lstlisting}

After extraction, install \texttt{python-flint==0.9.0} in a Python
environment and run the included verification command. No network
access is needed during the certificate calculation. The verifier
first confirms data identity, then performs the rational-polynomial
checks and the zero-index checks. A successful run reports each
dimension separately. The hashes are provenance and integrity checks;
the mathematical proof is the zero-polynomial calculation together
with Theorem~\ref{thm:certificate}.

\subsection{What is and is not concluded}
All nine dimensions asked for in Chen--Kauers Problem~17 are covered,
with the original coefficients and the original sequence. No
additional hypothesis on $n$, dimension, arithmetic, or asymptotics
is imposed. This is an unconditional computer-assisted proof in the
ordinary exact-arithmetic sense, not a proof checked by a formal
proof assistant.

The result does not prove that order $d$ is minimal in every
dimension, does not settle a numbered Erd\H{o}s problem, and does not
establish that this work outranks unrelated results in the supplied
corpus. The request for a historically unprecedented principle is
also stronger than what is established here: the reduction has been
explicitly credited to its existing source. The precisely achieved
advance is the certification of the previously conjectured original
equations throughout the specified finite range.

\appendix
\section{Executable certificate construction}\label{app:code}
The following code is the standalone verification core included with
the source payload. Polynomial arithmetic is exact. Its recursive
moment elimination implements \eqref{eq:lower} and \eqref{eq:mu};
the explicit assertion on the discarded $-d$ coordinate checks the
boundary cancellation. The construction of the shifted vectors
implements \eqref{eq:AB}--\eqref{eq:W}, and the final loop checks
\eqref{eq:residual} and the separate zero-index identity.

\begin{lstlisting}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact verification of the ORIGINAL Kauers--Zeilberger rook recurrences.

Requires Python 3 and python-flint. No workspace imports or network access.
Usage: python transfer_rook_standalone.py --data transfer_rook_certificate_data.json
The data may instead be a ZIP containing certificate_data.json.

Checks source SHA256 hashes, strictly parses each original Maple recurrence,
compares all expanded integer coefficient vectors with the canonical data,
and checks exact polynomial identities in Q[n]. This is not sequence fitting.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import re
import time
import zipfile
from math import comb
from flint import fmpq as Fraction, fmpq_poly, fmpz_poly

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ArithmeticError(message)

def coefficient_bytes(coefficients):
    """Canonical bytes: json.dumps(list-of-lists), ASCII, no terminal newline."""
    return json.dumps(coefficients, ensure_ascii=True).encode('ascii')

def digest(blob):
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()

def safe_polynomial(expression, variable):
    """Interpret integer polynomial syntax; never execute source code."""
    def evaluate(node):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and type(node.value) is int:
            return node.value
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == 'n':
            return variable
        if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.USub, ast.UAdd)):
            value = evaluate(node.operand)
            return -value if isinstance(node.op, ast.USub) else value
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            left, right = evaluate(node.left), evaluate(node.right)
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
                return left + right
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
                return left - right
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
                return left * right
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Pow) and type(right) is int and 0 <= right <= 1000:
                return left ** right
        raise ValueError('Unsupported polynomial syntax: ' + ast.dump(node))
    clean = expression.replace('^', '**').replace('\n', ' ').strip()
    return evaluate(ast.parse(clean, mode='eval').body)

def parse_original(d, source_text):
    if d <= 9:
        marker = f'RRope[{d}]:='
        require(source_text.count(marker) == 1, f'd={d}: ambiguous source marker')
        body = source_text.split(marker, 1)[1].split(':', 1)[0]
    else:
        body = source_text.strip().rstrip(':;')
    body = body.replace('\\\n', '')
    variable = fmpz_poly([0, 1])
    coefficients = [None] * (d + 1)
    end = 0
    for match in re.finditer(r'f\[([^]]+)\]', body):
        index = fmpz_poly(safe_polynomial(match.group(1), variable))
        j = int(index(0))
        require(index == fmpz_poly([j, 1]), f'd={d}: index is not exactly n+j')
        require(0 <= j <= d, f'd={d}: invalid shift {j}')
        require(coefficients[j] is None, f'd={d}: duplicate shift {j}')
        expression = body[end:match.start()].strip()
        require(expression.endswith('*'), f'd={d}: missing coefficient product')
        coefficients[j] = fmpz_poly(safe_polynomial(expression[:-1], variable))
        end = match.end()
    require(not body[end:].strip(), f'd={d}: unparsed trailing source')
    require(all(p is not None for p in coefficients), f'd={d}: missing shift')
    require(coefficients[d] != 0, f'd={d}: leading coefficient is zero')
    return coefficients

def rook_initial_values(d, maximum):
    """Direct composition formula using integer polynomial arithmetic.

    G_n(s)=sum_{k=1}^n binom(n-1,k-1)*(n!/k!)*s^k.
    A_d(n)=sum_K [s^K]G_n(s)^d*K!/(n!)^d; A_d(0)=1.
    """
    factorials = [1]
    for k in range(1, d * maximum + 1):
        factorials.append(k * factorials[-1])
    values = [1]
    for n in range(1, maximum + 1):
        g = fmpz_poly([0] + [comb(n - 1, k - 1) *
                            (factorials[n] // factorials[k])
                            for k in range(1, n + 1)])
        numerator = sum(int(c) * factorials[k] for k, c in enumerate(g ** d))
        denominator = factorials[n] ** d
        require(numerator % denominator == 0, 'Nonintegral direct rook number')
        values.append(numerator // denominator)
    return values

def cleared_vectors(d, jmax=None):
    """Return W[j][b] with P_j(n)^d A_d(n+j)=sum_b W[j][b] J_n(0,b).

    P_j=product_{h=1}^j(n+h), b runs from 1-d through 0.
    All computations are exact in Q[n]; only constant divisions occur.
    """
    n0 = fmpq_poly([0,1])
    if jmax is None:
        jmax = d
    memo = {}
    cdiag = [Fraction(1)]
    for i in range(d):
        cdiag.append(cdiag[-1]*Fraction(1+i, d-i))
    def add(u, v, c=1):
        w = dict(u)
        for key, val in v.items():
            w[key] = w.get(key, 0) + c*val
        return {kk: vv for kk, vv in w.items() if vv != 0}
    def scale(u, c):
        return {kk: c*vv for kk, vv in u.items() if c*vv != 0}
    def low(i, k):
        key = ('low', i, k)
        if key in memo:
            return memo[key]
        if i == 0:
            res = {}
        else:
            part = scale(low(i-1, k), i)
            part = add(part, scale(J(i-1, k-1), -k))
            if i >= 2:
                part = add(part, scale(J(i-2, k-1), -(i-1)*n0))
            res = scale(part, Fraction(1, d-i+1))
        memo[key] = res
        return res
    def J0(k):
        key = ('J0', k)
        if key in memo:
            return memo[key]
        if k <= 0:
            require(k >= -d, 'Invalid base moment')
            res = {k: Fraction(1)}
        else:
            rhs = add(scale(J(d, k-1), k), scale(J(d-1, k-1), d*n0))
            rhs = scale(rhs, Fraction(1, 1+d))
            res = scale(add(rhs, low(d, k), -1), 1/cdiag[d])
        memo[key] = res
        return res
    def J(i, k):
        key = ('J', i, k)
        if key in memo:
            return memo[key]
        require(k >= i - d, 'Invalid reduced moment')
        if i == 0:
            res = J0(k)
        else:
            res = add(scale(J0(k), cdiag[i]), low(i, k))
        memo[key] = res
        return res
    # Cleared shift polynomials A_j,B_j,C_j,D_j, represented in powers of s.
    def padd(p, q):
        r = [Fraction(0)]*max(len(p), len(q))
        for i, x in enumerate(p): r[i] += x
        for i, x in enumerate(q): r[i] += x
        return r
    def pmul(p, q):
        r = [Fraction(0)]*(len(p)+len(q)-1)
        for i, x in enumerate(p):
            if x:
                for j, y in enumerate(q):
                    if y:
                        r[i+j] += x*y
        return r
    vecs = []
    a, b, ap, bp = [Fraction(1)], [Fraction(0)], [Fraction(0)], [Fraction(1)]
    for j in range(jmax+1):
        if j > 0:
            m = n0 + j - 1
            # P_j*l_{n+j}=a*l_n+b*l_n'; P_j*l_{n+j}'=ap*l_n+bp*l_n'.
            na = [x for x in padd(pmul([m, Fraction(1)], a), pmul([Fraction(0), Fraction(1)], ap))]
            nb = [x for x in padd(pmul([m, Fraction(1)], b), pmul([Fraction(0), Fraction(1)], bp))]
            nap = [(m+1)*x for x in padd(a, ap)]
            nbp = [(m+1)*x for x in padd(b, bp)]
            a, b, ap, bp = na, nb, nap, nbp
        tot = {}
        for i in range(d+1):
            # binom(d,i) a^{d-i} b^i
            P = [Fraction(comb(d, i))]
            for _ in range(d-i):
                P = pmul(P, a)
            for _ in range(i):
                P = pmul(P, b)
            for k, c in enumerate(P):
                if c:
                    for key, val in J(i, k).items():
                        tot[key] = tot.get(key, 0) + c*val
        require(tot.get(-d, 0) == 0, f'd={d}, j={j}: forbidden boundary moment')
        vecs.append([tot.get(k, Fraction(0)) for k in range(1-d, 1)])
    return vecs

def load_data(path):
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
            return json.loads(archive.read('certificate_data.json'))
    return json.loads(path.read_bytes())

def check_dimension(d, data):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    record = data['recurrences'][str(d)]
    source = data['sources'][record['source']]
    source_bytes = source['text'].encode('ascii')
    require(digest(source_bytes) == source['sha256'], f'd={d}: source digest mismatch')
    K = parse_original(d, source['text'])
    coefficients = [[int(c) for c in polynomial] for polynomial in K]
    require(coefficients == record['coefficients'], f'd={d}: original coefficients mismatch')
    require(digest(coefficient_bytes(coefficients)) == record['coefficient_sha256'],
            f'd={d}: coefficient digest mismatch')
    W = cleared_vectors(d)
    P = [fmpq_poly([1])]
    for j in range(1, d + 1):
        P.append(P[-1] * fmpq_poly([j, 1]))
    for b in range(d):
        residual = fmpq_poly([0])
        for j in range(d + 1):
            quotient, remainder = divmod(P[d], P[j])
            require(remainder == 0, 'Unexpected denominator remainder')
            residual += fmpq_poly(K[j]) * quotient ** d * W[j][b]
        require(residual == 0, f'd={d}: nonzero residual at b={b + 1 - d}')
    # The integral/moment proof starts at n=1; n=0 is a separate exact check.
    # n=1,2 are additional independent finite-sum sanity checks.
    values = rook_initial_values(d, d + 2)
    for n in (0, 1, 2):
        require(sum(K[j](n) * values[n+j] for j in range(d + 1)) == 0,
                f'd={d}: failed direct recurrence check at n={n}')
    result = {
        'dimension': d,
        'order': d,
        'coefficient_degree': max(p.degree() for p in K),
        'max_coefficient_bits': max(abs(c).bit_length() for p in coefficients for c in p),
        'coefficient_sha256': record['coefficient_sha256'],
        'source_sha256': source['sha256'],
        'symbolic_residual_zero_count': d,
        'direct_initial_checks': [0, 1, 2],
        'seconds': time.perf_counter() - start,
    }
    print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
    return result

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--data', type=Path,
                        default=Path(__file__).with_name('transfer_rook_certificate_data.json'))
    parser.add_argument('--dimensions', type=int, nargs='+', default=list(range(2, 13)))
    parser.add_argument('--report', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--extract-sources', type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    require(all(2 <= d <= 12 for d in args.dimensions), 'Dimensions must be between 2 and 12')
    data = load_data(args.data)
    require(data['format'] == 'rook-exact-certificate-v1', 'Unrecognized data format')
    if args.extract_sources:
        args.extract_sources.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for filename, source in data['sources'].items():
            require(Path(filename).name == filename, 'Unsafe embedded filename')
            args.extract_sources.joinpath(filename).write_bytes(source['text'].encode('ascii'))
    report = [check_dimension(d, data) for d in args.dimensions]
    if args.report:
        args.report.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
    print('PASS: exact original-coefficient recurrence identities for dimensions ' +
          ', '.join(map(str, args.dimensions)), flush=True)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
\end{lstlisting}
